# Vendored Minutes contract — provenance

## `minutes-frontmatter.schema.json`

Byte-identical copy of the frontmatter schema published by the consumer of this tool's output.

| | |
|---|---|
| Source | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/silverstein/minutes/main/schema/meeting.schema.json` |
| Canonical `$id` | `https://useminutes.app/schema/meeting.schema.json` |
| Upstream version | Minutes 0.25.1 (workspace `Cargo.toml`) |
| Vendored on | 2026-08-16 |
| SHA-256 | `7a0bbf244992aa814de9359420c5dae4d572335bc589b1188190666a3c15f499` |

**Do not edit this file.** It is a vendored artifact, kept byte-identical so
`.github/workflows/contract-drift.yml` can diff it against upstream without noise.
To refresh it, see [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../CONTRIBUTING.md#refreshing-the-vendored-minutes-schema).

## Why there are two schemas here

Upstream has **two different `Frontmatter` structs**, and the published schema tracks neither
perfectly:

| Artifact | Struct | Properties | `required` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema/meeting.schema.json` (vendored here) | hand-maintained | 18 | `title, type, date, duration` |
| `crates/core/src/snapshots/…json_schema_generates_valid_schema.snap` | `minutes_core::markdown::Frontmatter` via `minutes schema` | 32 | `title, type, date` |
| `crates/reader/src/types.rs` | `minutes_reader::types::Frontmatter` | — | `duration` is non-`Option` |

We validate against the **published** schema because it is the only artifact upstream ships with
an `$id`, and its `required` list matches the *reader* crate — the code that actually parses the
files this tool writes. It is the correct contract floor.

But the published file is a **lagging** indicator: nothing in upstream's repo regenerates it, and it
is currently missing 14 properties that the generated snapshot has — including `speaker_map`, the
field Minutes' own README credits this tool for. That is why:

- `speaker-map.overlay.json` exists (below), and
- the drift workflow watches the **snapshot** and `crates/reader/src/types.rs` as well, not just the
  published file. Watching only the published file would report "in sync" indefinitely while the real
  contract moved.

## `speaker-map.overlay.json`

Hand-written, transcribed from `crates/reader/src/types.rs` (`SpeakerAttribution`, `Confidence`,
`AttributionSource`). Covers the one field we emit that the vendored schema has no property for.

Its `source` enum is deliberately **closed** to upstream's six named variants. Upstream's
`AttributionSource` has an untagged `Unknown(String)` fallback so hand-edited files stay readable,
but *this tool* only ever emits `deterministic` (see `SPEAKERS` in `src/config.ts`). Validating our
own output against the closed set is a correct tightening: if we ever emit something else, that is a
bug on our side, not a contract change on theirs.
